lines.li: [them] When our horn sounds, the elders will look for your spears among ours.
[us,tribal] They'll be there, a clan that gives its word keeps it.
[us] They'll be there, we swore to it.
[them] Good, a promise made to the elders is never forgotten.
[them] Your colony pays its tithe like one of our old villages, without being chased for it.
[us] We'd rather not be chased.
[them] Aye, and our bailiff is glad of one gate there's no need to shout at.
[them] As far as the union's concerned, your colony pays its dues like a member.
[us] Do we get a vote, then?
[them] No, but you get the protection, which is what most members want anyway.
[them] Under the accord, your colony is listed as a protected party, second class.
[us] Who's first class?
[them] Our own settlements, and the shareholders.
[us] Our elders say a small clan that pays a strong one sleeps through the night.
[them,their:tribal] Ours say the same, from the other side of the fire.
[them] And mostly it does.
[us] Fealty sits easier on some of us than on others.
[them] It sits easiest on those who've seen a raid.
[us,colony:raid] Then it sits easy on all of us this season.
[us] Then give it time.
[us] Being a protectorate means more paperwork than I expected.
[them] It means a lot of things, and the paperwork is the easy part.
[us] Our charter puts us under your protection, but the raiders haven't read it.
[them,fealty:protected] Our band explained it to them this season, I'm told.
[them] That's what our band is for.
[them] Our collector likes your gate best in the fall, when the stores are full.
[us] We like the fall too, for the same reason.
[them] Then we understand each other.
[them] Your tribute reached our collector in full again, and our head noticed.
[us] We keep our side.
[them] Not everyone who holds of us does.
[them] At home they call this place one of ours now.
[us] One of yours, or one that holds of you?
[them] At home they don't bother with the difference.
[them] My head sent me partly to see how the people who hold of us live.
[us] And how do we live?
[them] Better than some, and you keep your walls up.
[them] When I hold my people's seat, your oath will be to me.
[us] Then I hope we'll get on as well as we do now.
[them] Better, if you're wise.
[them] It's easier to hold of people who pray as you do, I think.
[us] Some of ours said as much when we swore.
[them] They were right.
[them] We're at war, so don't be surprised if our head calls on your oath.
[us] We know the terms.
[them] Knowing them and keeping them are different things.
[them] Our collector says your tribute fell short this season.
[us] It was all the stores could give.
[them] Then the stores had better fill up.
[them] Our head knows it was a lean season for you, and so do I.
[us] We'll make it up as soon as we can.
[them] Make it up before our collector comes again, and nobody will say a word.
[them] I'd rather speak of your tribute here than write about it.
[us] We'll send what's owed as soon as the stores allow.
[them] See that you do, I'd hate to see the oath broken over a cart of goods.
[us] A poor colony feels every coin of its tribute.
[them] A poor colony needs our band more than a rich one.
[us] I know, and I still feel every coin.
[them] Your colony fell short once, and paid it in the end.
[us] We did, and we'd rather not again.
[them] Our collector remembers it, all the same.
[them] Our head called on your oath this season, as the terms allow.
[us] We read that letter twice before we answered it.
[them] Most do.
[them] The young warriors still talk about your spears at our fire.
[us] Ours still talk about it too.
[them] Then it was a fight worth sharing.
[them] Our captain says your levies held their ground better than some of ours.
[us] Don't let your own hear you say that.
[them] They've heard it, and they're sulking.
[them] Your people showed up when we called and did the job, which is all we ask.
[us] Our people did more than a job.
[them] They did, and it's in the report.
[them] Our fighters remember the ones your colony sent when we called.
[us] We remember the road there.
[them] Long, I hear, and longer coming back.
[us] We haven't forgotten your band walking in when the raiders were at our walls.
[them,their:tribal] Our warriors still sing about it, badly.
[them] Nor have they, they still talk about it.
[us] Tell them they're welcome at our table.
[them] Our band came home from your walls proud of what they did.
[us] They should be, they stood with us.
[them] They say your people stood just as well.
[them] Our band came when you were raided, so I trust the tribute stays honest.
[us] It will.
[them] Good.
[them] Our response team marked your raid as handled, and it was.
[us] It was, with their help.
[them] That's the service, and you pay for it.
[them] Your colony swore to us, and then it unswore.
[us] It wasn't an easy choice.
[them] It was easy enough to make.
[them] Oath-breakers shouldn't expect a welcome anywhere.
[us] We didn't come looking for one.
[them] At home they still talk about the colony that walked out of its oath.
[us] We had our reasons.
[them] Everyone has reasons.
[them] Among our people, an oath given back is remembered longer than one kept.
[us] Then we'll be remembered a long time.
[them] You will.
[them] Your colony walked out of its contract with us, and our office kept the copy.
[us] Keep it, we have ours.
[them] Ours has notes in the margin.
[them] Your colony leaving the oath stung, but I don't hold it against you.
[us] That's more than I expected.
[them] Some of us remember other things about your colony too.
[us] Last time you told me about {THEN}, and now I hear {NOW} leads you.
[them] {NOW} does, and will expect your tribute just as {THEN} did.
[us] It'll come, as it always has.
[us] Your war with {THEN} is over, I hear.
[them] Over, and our head can stop thinking about calling on your oath for it.
[us] We'd have come.
[them] I know, and so does our head.
[them] Our kin sent their harvest up to your gate, as the terms say.
[us,vassal:heavy] It was a heavy share, I know.
[us] It came, and it was welcome.
[them,vassal:heavy] Heavy is the word they used too.
[them] They were glad to have it to send.
[them] Our kin say your colony asks a fair share of their harvest, and no more.
[us] We'd rather they did well than paid much.
[them] They do well, and they say so.
[them] Our kin eat less so your colony can eat more.
[us] Protection costs, on both sides.
[them] It costs one side more.
[them] Our kin ran the numbers on your harvest share, and they don't like them.
[us] Numbers rarely please anyone.
[them] These seem to please your colony well enough.
[them] Our kin left their fields to fight at your walls when you called.
[us] And we were glad of every one of them.
[them,their:lowtech] Then see they go home with something to show for it.
[them] Then see they're thanked properly.
[them] Your colony calls our kin to its fights, and they pay for it.
[us] They're paid back in protection.
[them] So you keep saying.
[them] The share your council takes from our harvest is a heavy one, and we feel it.
[us] I'll tell the council what you said.
[them] Tell them we're still standing, but only just.
[them] When your call came, our people picked up whatever they had and went.
[us] We were glad to see them come.
[them] We'd do it again, if it came to that.
[them] When our kin asked for help, your colony sent it, and they haven't forgotten.
[us] They hold of us, so we look after them.
[them] That's how it should go, and it doesn't always.
[us] The clan's spear stands over your kin, as long as we stand.
[them] They feel it, and sleep the better for it.
[us] Your kin are under our protection, and we'd march out for them.
[them,vassal:levy] They marched for you this season, so it's only fair.
[them] They'd want to see it before they believed it.
[us] Your kin's town is a protectorate of ours, with the guarantee in writing.
[them] Writing is easy, it's the guarantee they care about.
[us] Your kin are under our charter of protection, fully covered.
[them] Covered against what, exactly?
[us] Raiders, mostly, and bad seasons when we can manage it.
[them] Our kin asked your colony for help, and found themselves with a liege.
[us] With protection, which is what they asked for.
[them] We'll see what it costs them in the end.
[them] Lording it over our kin doesn't make your colony a lord.
[us] We never said it did.
[them] Our kin write home that they sleep easier under your protection.
[us] That's what we hoped for.
[them,vassal:heavy] They'd sleep easier still with a lighter cart at harvest.
[them] Then you'll be glad to hear it.
[them] Our kin under your spear hunt where they like now, and the elders say it's good.
[us] Then they're doing well.
[them] Well enough to grumble about the share you take, so very well.
[them] Our kin under your protection pay their dues and still keep a market day.
[us] Good, a town needs its market.
[them] Aye, and a market needs a safe road.
[them] Our kin's settlement is doing better under your guarantee, the figures show it.
[us] What figures?
[them] The ones they send home to us every season.
